title: Distribution, Research, and Pricing - Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA - Channel Management
subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of channel management in marketing?
options: To create new products based on consumer trends
To determine the best way to move products from producer to consumer
To design the promotional campaigns for a product
To set the baseline price of a new service
questions.explain: Channel management, or distribution, focuses on the strategies and processes used to move products efficiently from the manufacturer or producer to the final consumer.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A distribution channel in which the producer sells directly to the final consumer without any intermediaries is known as:
options: Indirect distribution
Wholesale distribution
Direct distribution
Intensive distribution
questions.explain: Direct distribution occurs when the producer sells goods or services directly to the customer, with no middlemen involved.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following intermediaries typically buys large quantities of goods from manufacturers, stores them, and resells them to retailers?
options: Brokers
Retailers
Agents
Wholesalers
questions.explain: Wholesalers are intermediaries who buy in bulk from producers and sell smaller quantities to retailers for consumer distribution.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: If a company like Coca-Cola wants its products to be available in as many outlets as possible (e.g., supermarkets, gas stations, vending machines), which distribution strategy are they using?
options: Exclusive distribution
Selective distribution
Intensive distribution
Direct distribution
questions.explain: Intensive distribution aims to provide maximum market coverage by selling a product through all suitable and available wholesalers or retailers.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A high-end luxury watch brand restricts the sale of its watches to only one specific authorized dealer in a major city. What kind of distribution strategy is this?
options: Exclusive distribution
Selective distribution
Intensive distribution
Horizontal distribution
questions.explain: Exclusive distribution involves severely limiting the number of intermediaries, often granting a single outlet the exclusive rights to sell a product in a geographic area to maintain brand prestige.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which channel intermediary never takes legal ownership (title) of the goods, but instead merely facilitates the sale between buyers and sellers?
options: Merchant wholesaler
Agent or Broker
Retailer
Industrial distributor
questions.explain: Agents and brokers negotiate sales and bring buyers and sellers together, earning a commission, but they do not take ownership (title) of the products.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which distribution strategy falls between intensive and exclusive, using a limited number of outlets in a given geographic area to sell products like electronics or clothing?
options: Direct distribution
Selective distribution
Wholesale distribution
Franchise distribution
questions.explain: Selective distribution uses a few select outlets in an area. It is typically used for shopping goods where consumers spend time comparing prices and features.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) is primarily used in channel management to:
options: Send automated consumer marketing emails
Process digital payments from end consumers
Exchange business documents, like purchase orders and invoices, automatically between companies
Track the GPS location of delivery trucks
questions.explain: EDI is the computer-to-computer exchange of business documents in a standard electronic format between business partners, which streamlines the supply chain.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: How does Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology improve channel management?
options: It completely replaces the need for online shopping carts
It allows businesses to track inventory locations in real-time through radio waves
It provides detailed psychographic profiles of customers walking into stores
It handles the payroll processing for warehouse employees
questions.explain: RFID tags emit radio signals that can be read by scanners, allowing companies to accurately and automatically track inventory as it moves through the supply chain.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: When a manufacturer bypasses its traditional retail intermediaries to sell directly to consumers online, this is an example of:
options: Horizontal integration
Disintermediation
Selective allocation
Reverse distribution
questions.explain: Disintermediation is the removal of intermediaries in a supply chain, often facilitated by the internet allowing producers to sell directly to consumers.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Vertical channel conflict typically occurs between:
options: Two retailers selling the same product in the same town
Two rival manufacturers making competing products
Different levels of the same channel, such as a manufacturer and a retailer
Consumers arguing over limited stock items
questions.explain: Vertical channel conflict involves disagreements between members at different levels of the same distribution channel, like a producer and a wholesaler.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What type of conflict occurs when two different franchisees of the same fast-food chain in the same city are arguing over territorial boundaries?
options: Vertical channel conflict
Horizontal channel conflict
Inter-brand conflict
Direct distribution conflict
questions.explain: Horizontal channel conflict occurs among members at the same level of the distribution channel, such as two retailers or two franchisees.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What role does an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system play in channel management?
options: It primarily generates television commercials.
It integrates internal and external management information across an entire organization, optimizing inventory and supply chain operations.
It surveys consumers about their satisfaction with customer service.
It physically transports goods from the factory to the retail store.
questions.explain: An ERP integrates various business processes—like inventory, sales, and supply chain management—into a single system, improving information flow and channel efficiency.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What is 'reverse logistics' in channel management?
options: Selling a product at a lower price than competitors
The process of moving goods from their typical final destination back to the producer, for reasons like returns or recycling
When a retailer dictates production schedules to a manufacturer
Transporting raw materials from suppliers to the factory
questions.explain: Reverse logistics refers to all operations related to the reuse of products and materials, including customer returns, recycling, and refurbishing.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an indirect channel of distribution?
options: A farmer selling vegetables at a local farmer's market
A jewelry maker selling handmade items on their own website
A manufacturer selling cars through franchised, independent dealerships
A baker delivering fresh bread directly to a neighbor's house
questions.explain: An indirect channel involves one or more intermediaries. The dealership acts as an intermediary between the car manufacturer and the consumer.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: How do Extranets primarily benefit channel members?
options: By allowing the general public to buy wholesale products
By providing a secure, private network that allows authorized partners, suppliers, and buyers to share information and collaborate
By scanning barcodes at the point of sale
By physically managing the warehouse layout
questions.explain: An Extranet extends a company's intranet to authorized external users (like channel partners), facilitating secure sharing of inventory and order information.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Physical distribution (logistics) focuses primarily on:
options: Deciding which advertising media to use
Transportation, warehousing, materials handling, and inventory control
Calculating profit margins on retail goods
Developing the branding for a new product line
questions.explain: Physical distribution encompasses the physical movement of goods, including transport, storage, handling, and inventory tracking.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Why might a manufacturer choose to use intermediaries rather than selling directly to all consumers?
options: Intermediaries always decrease the final price for the consumer.
Manufacturers lack the expertise, infrastructure, and financial resources to efficiently reach all individual consumers.
It is legally required to use intermediaries in all industries.
Direct distribution results in lower profit margins per unit.
questions.explain: Intermediaries add efficiency by providing storage, sales forces, market reach, and logistics that the manufacturer might not possess or find cost-effective to develop.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What does a 'B2B' channel of distribution entail?
options: Business-to-Business, where goods are sold from one business to another for operational use or further production
Business-to-Consumer, where goods are sold directly to the final individual user
Broker-to-Broker, an exchange exclusively between independent agents
Buyer-to-Buyer, a peer-to-peer selling network
questions.explain: B2B stands for Business-to-Business. In these channels, organizations sell products and services to other organizations rather than individual end consumers.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which technology allows retailers to automatically order more stock from a supplier when an item’s inventory level drops to a certain point?
options: Computer-Aided Design (CAD)
Automated Inventory Replenishment system
Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system
Search Engine Optimization (SEO)
questions.explain: Automated inventory replenishment systems use POS data to automatically generate purchase orders when stock levels hit a predetermined minimum.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA
